dedupe_keys.name: database of material degradation events in the process industry 1966 2023

description: This database lists 3,772 incidents caused by material degradation in the process industry between 1966 and 2023, drawn from the main European and American open-access incident databases. The Mendeley Data record says material degradation, such as corrosion, erosion, fatigue and ageing, causes about 30 percent of substance releases in the process industry, and that each event is classified with a systematic scheme of causes and consequences consistent with the authors' earlier work. It was published on 9 April 2025 by Morena Vitale, David Javier Castro Rodriguez, Antonello Barresi and Micaela Demichela as one downloadable Excel file of about 336 KB, free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is worldwide as far as the source databases report, mostly Europe and the United States. Caveats: the source databases are not named on the page read, and reporting bias in those databases carries over. For simulation it gives failure causes and consequences of ageing equipment to set degradation-driven failure rates and release scenarios in process plant risk models. Related catalogue records include the Natech lightning events dataset (same group), the China industrial corrosion failure cases and eMARS.
